title: A Case for Speculative Address Translation with Rapid Validation for GPUs
problem: GPU address translation faces high TLB pressure in heterogeneous systems with irregular and memory-intensive applications, causing up to 34.5% performance slowdown due to translation latency overhead.
motivation: Unified address spaces are essential for heterogeneous systems to enable efficient data sharing between CPUs and GPUs.
method: Avatar speeds up GPU memory requests by speculatively translating addresses (predicting which physical memory location each virtual address maps to) before the translation is official. It uses CAST (Contiguity-Aware Speculative Translation) to predict translations by monitoring which pages are adjacent in memory, allowing the GPU to fetch data immediately while the real translation happens in parallel. CAVA (In-Cache Validation) validates these predictions by storing page-mapping information in 32-byte sectors within 128-byte cache lines, enabling near-instantaneous verification at the sector level.
key_novelty: By validating speculative address translations through metadata embedded in cache sectors, Avatar lets GPUs fetch data and do address translation at the same time—without special hardware support.
contributions: Identifies contiguous page patterns for predicting virtual-to-physical address mapping in GPU memory systems
Proposes CAST mechanism enabling speculative GPU address translation with background validation
Proposes CAVA mechanism for rapid speculation validation using embedded cache sector metadata
Achieves 37.2% average GPU performance improvement with 90.3% speculation accuracy
limitations: Abstract does not discuss limitations; applicability to sequential workloads or other GPU architectures not addressed.
primary_theme: GPU address translation acceleration via speculation
